catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: General and structural pass covering layering, domain modeling, registries, provider adapters, file-based knowledge storage, CI validation, and observability. Agentic orchestration, prompt design, and agent-role patterns were omitted.
analysis_limits: Only the directory tree, manifest snippet, and symbol lists were available; full file contents were not inspected.
Some patterns are inferred from module placement and symbol names rather than executed behavior.
Agentic-specific components were not analyzed and are deliberately excluded from this catalogue.

system_map.overview: The repository is a Python package named cas_runner under src/, organized around a CLI entrypoint, a FlowRunner orchestrator, governance and steering domain modules, LLM provider clients, a dashboard health model, a file-based cas-knowledge store, CI validation scripts, and documentation/portal assets. The structural emphasis is on typed domain models, registry-driven governance behavior, provider abstraction, and directory-convention persistence for architectural knowledge artifacts.

patterns.name: Src-layout layered CLI runner architecture
patterns.summary: The Python package under src/cas_runner separates CLI, runner, governance, steering, LLM provider, dashboard, and bootstrap modules, forming a layered CLI application layout.
patterns.intent: Separate invocation, orchestration, domain logic, and infrastructure clients into replaceable modules.
patterns.context: A command-line Python tool that coordinates governance and steering behavior without a web service boundary.
forces: Avoid import cycles between CLI, domain, and infrastructure
Allow independent evolution of governance, steering, and provider logic
Keep CLI surface thin and testable
patterns.solution: Use a src layout with main in cli.py, FlowRunner in runner.py, domain modules under governance and steering, and infrastructure clients under llm.
implementation_signals: Package modules are localized under src/cas_runner
cli.py exposes main while runner.py exposes FlowRunner
Domain and infrastructure concerns occupy separate subpackages

evidence.note: Command-line entrypoint separate from runner logic.
Runner class suggests an application-layer orchestration boundary.

benefits: Clear ownership boundary between invocation and execution
Easier replacement of runners, providers, or knowledge stores
Module boundaries improve navigation
costs: More modules to bootstrap and understand
Risk of FlowRunner accumulating too many use cases
failure_modes: FlowRunner becomes a god orchestrator
Infrastructure clients leak into domain models

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful when a CLI application needs to separate user-facing entrypoints from use-case runners and domain engines.

patterns.name: Pydantic governance domain modeling
patterns.summary: Governance entities, metrics, findings, and actions are represented as typed record models in a dedicated models module.
patterns.intent: Provide validated, serializable, and consistent representations of governance state.
patterns.context: The governance subsystem needs stable contracts for inventory, health, throughput, risk, compliance, and actions.
forces: Data must be validated at boundaries
Domain concepts need a shared vocabulary
Models should be usable for metrics, findings, and persistence
patterns.solution: Centralize governance record types in src/cas_runner/governance/models.py using Pydantic-style models and a domain exception type.
implementation_signals: Multiple record symbols are colocated in governance/models.py
Compliance and governance metrics are modeled explicitly
A dedicated GovernanceException is present

evidence.note: Defines the core governance domain vocabulary.

benefits: Early validation of governance data
Stable module-to-module contracts
Readable domain language
costs: Model changes may ripple through engines and services
Central models file can grow large
failure_modes: Models encode infrastructure schema rather than domain concepts
Validation hides inconsistent workflow state

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable when a governance or policy system needs typed invariants before execution or persistence.

patterns.name: Steering capability and delta modeling
patterns.summary: Steering-related data is modeled as structured records for Git deltas, capability records, capability sets, lineage, and architectural deltas.
patterns.intent: Represent architectural change and capability context in a normalized, queryable form.
patterns.context: The steering subsystem needs to reason about repository changes and runtime capability indexes.
forces: Git changes must be normalized before analysis
Capability records need lineage and grouping
Architectural deltas need a stable payload shape
patterns.solution: Define enums and record models in src/cas_runner/steering/models.py for raw deltas, capability records, sets, lineage, and architectural deltas.
implementation_signals: RawGitDelta separates raw change data from derived concepts
CapabilitySet and CapabilityLineage suggest grouping and provenance
ArchitecturalDelta is a distinct derived model

evidence.note: Symbols include prompt-adjacent data fields, but the structural pattern is the data shape and normalization, not prompt orchestration.

benefits: Raw and derived data remain distinct
Capability provenance is easier to trace
Steering logic can consume stable payloads
costs: More model layers to populate
Delta normalization must stay in sync with Git source formats
failure_modes: Prompt-adjacent fields become uncontrolled free text
Raw deltas are consumed directly instead of normalized models

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful when change detection produces heterogeneous raw events that must be normalized into capability and delta records.

patterns.name: Transition registry governance state machine
patterns.summary: A TransitionRegistry paired with GovernanceActionEngine suggests that governance transitions are registered explicitly and applied by an engine.
patterns.intent: Make allowed governance state transitions explicit and centralize action execution.
patterns.context: Governance actions likely have lifecycle states that must not be bypassed or misordered.
forces: Illegal transitions must be rejected
Transition rules should be auditable
New action types should be addable without broad code changes
patterns.solution: Register transitions in a TransitionRegistry and let GovernanceActionEngine validate and apply actions against that registry.
implementation_signals: A registry-specific symbol exists next to an engine symbol
Governance action logic is separated from generic runner logic

evidence.note: Registry and engine symbols imply registry-driven transition handling.

benefits: Central place to audit permitted transitions
Easier extension of new governance actions
Separation of rules from execution mechanics
costs: Registry initialization becomes part of runtime configuration
Incomplete registry definitions can cause subtle failures
failure_modes: Transition registry bypassed by ad-hoc state mutation
Rules become too permissive and lose enforcement value

patterns.reuse_notes: Good fit for lifecycle domains where permitted state transitions are limited and auditable.

patterns.name: Governance action service use-case boundary
patterns.summary: GovernanceActionService provides an application-service boundary for governance actions, likely coordinating engines and models behind a use-case API.
patterns.intent: Expose governance action execution as a service API rather than exposing internal engine details.
patterns.context: Runners or CLI commands need to perform governance actions without directly managing transition registries or compliance engines.
forces: Callers need a simple API
Engines need internal coordination
Use-case effects should be observable or traceable
patterns.solution: Introduce GovernanceActionService as the service boundary that orchestrates governance engines and domain models.
implementation_signals: Service naming separates use-case execution from engine internals
Service sits alongside engine and model modules

benefits: Simplifies integration from CLI or runner
Encapsulates governance execution details
Easier to add cross-cutting checks around actions
costs: Another abstraction layer to maintain
Service may become a boundary bottleneck if overly generalized
failure_modes: Service wraps engines too loosely and becomes pass-through
Business rules leak from engine into service

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when domain engines are too detailed for presentation or orchestration callers.

patterns.name: Compliance engine finding and metrics modeling
patterns.summary: ComplianceEngine is paired with ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics models, indicating rule evaluation that produces structured findings and metrics.
patterns.intent: Separate compliance evaluation from action execution and express results as structured outputs.
patterns.context: Governance artifacts or actions must be evaluated against rules, with exceptions and metrics reported consistently.
forces: Rule outcomes must be machine-readable
Findings need provenance and severity
Metrics should be derivable from evaluation results
patterns.solution: Implement a compliance engine that consumes governance data and emits ComplianceFinding and ComplianceMetrics records.
implementation_signals: Engine class is separate from model definitions
Finding and metric symbols are colocated in governance/models.py

benefits: Rule results are inspectable and testable
Metrics can be derived from explicit findings
Compliance logic can be isolated from action execution
costs: Rule coverage must be maintained
Findings require stable schema interpretation
failure_modes: Findings become opaque to users
Engine embeds too many project-specific rule assumptions

patterns.reuse_notes: Suitable for policy systems where evaluation outputs need to feed dashboards, audits, or further automation.

patterns.name: LLM provider adapter and test double port
patterns.summary: LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient provide separate provider clients under an llm package, abstracting LLM transport from business logic.
patterns.intent: Decouple application and governance logic from a concrete LLM provider and enable deterministic testing.
patterns.context: The project depends on litellm and likely needs both real provider calls and fake responses for tests or dry runs.
forces: Real provider calls are expensive and nondeterministic
Tests need stable provider behavior
Provider APIs may change faster than domain logic
patterns.solution: Expose provider interaction through client classes: LiteLLMClient for production and MockLLMClient for testing or dry runs.
implementation_signals: Dedicated llm package
Real and mock client names
litellm dependency in pyproject.toml

benefits: Domains do not import provider libraries directly
Tests can avoid network and provider calls
Provider swaps are localized
costs: Mock behavior must remain representative enough to catch integration issues
Client port may need maintenance when provider semantics change
failure_modes: Mock client diverges from real client behavior
Prompt or retry logic leaks into providers

patterns.reuse_notes: This is a structural adapter/port choice for provider transport, distinct from agentic prompt or loop design.

patterns.name: Workspace bootstrap and governance block merging
patterns.summary: bootstrap.py defines init_workspace, bootstrap, and merge_cas_governance_block, indicating a structured setup path for target workspaces.
patterns.intent: Standardize initialization of a workspace and inject a CAS governance block in a controlled way.
patterns.context: The tool appears to operate across repositories or project workspaces that need governance metadata applied consistently.
forces: Projects need consistent setup
Governance metadata must be merged rather than overwritten blindly
Bootstrap behavior should be explicit and re-runnable
patterns.solution: Provide bootstrap functions that initialize a workspace and merge a governance block into the target configuration or repository state.
implementation_signals: Function names directly describe initialization and merging
Bootstrap is separated from runner and domain engines

evidence.note: Symbols indicate workspace initialization and governance block merging.

benefits: Onboarding projects can be scripted
Governance block can be applied consistently
Setup logic is inspectable in one module
costs: Merge semantics must be designed carefully
Bootstrap failures can block downstream execution
failure_modes: Idempotency is not guaranteed
Merge conflicts silently drop user modifications

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful when a tool needs to apply a standard governance or tooling block to many target repositories.

patterns.name: Derived health status and reasoning model
patterns.summary: The dashboard health model defines HealthStatus, calculate_health, and get_health_reasons, indicating health is derived from underlying signals.
patterns.intent: Produce a compact health status plus human-readable reasons from measured governance or system state.
patterns.context: Dashboards or CLI reports need to summarize health without exposing every underlying metric.
forces: Status should be consistent and reproducible
Reasons should explain status changes
Presentation should not compute raw metrics
patterns.solution: Encode health as an enum, calculate it from inputs, and generate reasons separately from the status value.
implementation_signals: Status is modeled as HealthStatus
Explicit calculate_health and get_health_reasons functions

benefits: Consistent status vocabulary
Reasons can be rendered independently
Health logic is testable without UI concerns
costs: Reason generation must stay aligned with calculation rules
Status thresholds may require tuning
failure_modes: Reason strings diverge from actual health calculation
Health status becomes a blunt summary that hides actionable detail

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable when reports need both a machine-friendly status and operator-friendly explanations.

patterns.name: File-based knowledge base layout
patterns.summary: cas-knowledge separates global, projects, runtime, and templates directories, forming a file-based architectural knowledge store.
patterns.intent: Persist architecture knowledge, governance rules, project contexts, runtime state, and artifact templates using filesystem conventions.
patterns.context: The system needs a portable, reviewable, and versionable store of non-code architectural artifacts.
forces: Knowledge must be inspectable by humans
Global and project scopes must not collide
Templates should guide new artifact creation
Runtime state should be separable from stable knowledge
patterns.solution: Organize cas-knowledge into global, projects, runtime, and templates subdirectories, with YAML and JSON files for machine-readable context and Markdown templates for human-authored artifacts.
implementation_signals: Directory names encode scope: global, projects, runtime, templates
Runtime files include execution-profile.yaml and rule-context.json
Templates exist for patterns, rules, signals, learning, and decisions

evidence.note: Global knowledge directory with decisions, governance, rules, patterns, and signals subdirectories.
Project-scoped knowledge directory with multiple project folders.
Templates for architecture and knowledge artifacts.

benefits: Knowledge is reviewable in source control
Scope separation reduces project interference
Templates reduce ad-hoc artifact authoring
costs: Path conventions become implicit contracts
Filesystem layout can be fragile without schemas
failure_modes: Modules hardcode paths instead of resolving layout through configuration
Runtime state is accidentally committed as stable knowledge

patterns.reuse_notes: Good fit for governance systems that need a human-reviewable artifact store alongside executable code.

patterns.name: CI workflow constraint suite
patterns.summary: validate_workflows.py implements named checks for workflow syntax, hardcoding, installer pinning, dry-run reachability, retired workflows, trigger remediation, and composite action adoption.
patterns.intent: Enforce structural and operational rules for CI workflows as executable quality gates.
patterns.context: The repository contains multiple CI workflows and a composite setup action, requiring consistent workflow architecture.
forces: Workflow YAML must remain syntactically valid
Hardcoded values should be discouraged
Installers should be pinned or otherwise controlled
Retired workflows and dry-run misconfiguration must be detected
patterns.solution: Implement a Python validator with check_* functions and a main entrypoint that can be run by CI to fail builds on workflow debt.
implementation_signals: Check functions are named by specific workflow constraint
Validator lives in a spec directory linked to CI simplification
CI workflows exist for validation, steering, governance, and portal publishing

evidence.note: Encodes workflow architecture rules as executable checks.
Composite action for CI environment setup.

benefits: Workflow architecture debt is tested automatically
Rules are discoverable through function names
CI changes are constrained without manual review alone
costs: Validators must be updated as workflow conventions evolve
Overly strict checks can slow workflow experimentation
failure_modes: Validator drifts from actual CI conventions
Checks are bypassed in non-default workflow paths

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for repositories where CI YAML is an architectural surface and should be linted like code.

patterns.name: OpenTelemetry trace pipeline integration
patterns.summary: OpenTelemetry API and SDK dependencies, together with a runtime traces directory, indicate structured observability integration.
patterns.intent: Capture execution traces and make runtime behavior inspectable outside the process.
patterns.context: Governance and steering runs likely produce side effects that need diagnostic tracing.
forces: Traces should be available without invasive logging
Provider and governance calls should be correlated
Trace artifacts should be stored in a predictable location
patterns.solution: Use OpenTelemetry libraries for instrumentation and store trace artifacts under cas-knowledge/runtime/traces/.
implementation_signals: opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk dependencies
Persistent traces directory in runtime knowledge area

benefits: Structured diagnostics for multistep execution
Trace storage can be retained for audits or debugging
Observability is separated from business logic
costs: Trace exporters and initialization require wiring
Trace retention may need lifecycle management
failure_modes: Traces are emitted but never collected
Sensitive prompts or payloads leak into trace artifacts

patterns.reuse_notes: Use when a CLI or batch system needs traceability without adding a centralized telemetry service.

patterns.name: Markdown template-driven knowledge capture
patterns.summary: cas-knowledge/templates contains Markdown templates for patterns, rules, signals, learning records, experiments, ADRs, and promotion decisions, standardizing knowledge capture.
patterns.intent: Reduce variation in how architectural learning artifacts are written and reviewed.
patterns.context: The project explicitly treats heuristics, patterns, signals, and decisions as first-class knowledge artifacts.
forces: Knowledge records need comparable sections
Promotion from heuristic to pattern needs traceable rationale
Templates should be easy to copy and minimize authoring friction
patterns.solution: Provide reusable Markdown templates under cas-knowledge/templates/ for each artifact type.
implementation_signals: Template filenames map directly to governance and knowledge concepts
Templates include pattern, rule, signal, learning, experiment, and promotion decision artifacts

evidence.note: Template for promoting heuristics to patterns.

benefits: Lower authoring cost for knowledge artifacts
Easier review due to consistent structure
Supports promotion and lineage workflows
costs: Templates may become stale as conventions evolve
Authors may fill templates with low-value boilerplate
failure_modes: Template structure hides important project-specific context
Templates are not validated against required sections

patterns.reuse_notes: Useful for any system that promotes informal learnings into reviewable architectural artifacts.

anti_patterns.name: Centralized governance model module concentration
symptoms: governance/models.py contains a large set of record types spanning inventory, health, throughput, risk, compliance, and actions
Multiple bounded concerns are colocated in one module
impact: Larger change surface for unrelated model updates
Potential coupling between metrics, findings, and action lifecycle models
Slower navigation as the module grows
suggested_remediation: Split models by aggregate or bounded context, such as compliance, health, metrics, and actions
Keep a compatibility import layer if public API stability is needed

anti_patterns.name: Documentation and specification proliferation
symptoms: Multiple high-level architecture, design, governance, runbook, AGENTS, CLAUDE, GEMINI, and spec documents exist
Similar lifecycle and governance concepts appear across docs, workflows, and templates
impact: Risk of drift between narrative documentation and executable behavior
Increased maintenance effort to keep multiple sources aligned
suggested_remediation: Designate canonical documents for each concern
Generate or link summary docs from executable specs and workflows
Add validation where documentation claims can be checked

anti_patterns.name: Implicit knowledge path conventions
symptoms: Knowledge store relies on fixed directories such as global/rules, projects/<project>, and runtime/traces
Available evidence does not show an explicit manifest or schema binding these paths to expected contents
impact: Migration or refactoring of the knowledge store can break runtime reads
New artifact types may not integrate cleanly
suggested_remediation: Introduce a manifest or layout configuration for cas-knowledge
Validate expected directory structure during bootstrap or CI
Centralize path constants in a dedicated module
